cues.en: In comparison, a stovetop kettle can only try its best at absorbing heat that's getting blasted at it from below
cues.zh: 相比之下，炉灶水壶只能尽最大努力去吸收从下方喷射过来的热量，

cues.en: and then transfer that heat into the water it contains.

cues.zh: 这比直接在水中释放热量的效率要低得多。

cues.en: How much less effective is it? Well, we can find out pretty easily with some math.
cues.zh: 它的效果会差多少？其实用一点数学就能很容易算出来。

cues.en: One fun thing about this universe is that energy is energy.
cues.zh: 这个宇宙有趣的一点是，能量就是能量。

cues.en: We have a lot of different names for it and measure it in a bunch of different ways, but it's all the same thing and we can convert between units easily.
cues.zh: 我们对它有好多不同的叫法，也用各种不同的方式来度量它，但它们其实是同一个东西，而且我们很容易就能在不同单位之间换算。

cues.en: One of those units which is particularly useful for this discussion is the calorie.
cues.zh: 这些单位中有一个对本次讨论特别有用，那就是卡路里。

cues.en: That's how much energy it takes to elevate the temperature of one cubic centimeter or one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius.
cues.zh: 这就是把一立方厘米（也就是一毫升）的水升高一摄氏度所需的能量。

cues.en: If we presume that the water from the tap is at about 20 degrees Celsius and we have 1,000 cubic centimeters of water to raise up by 80 degrees,
cues.zh: 如果我们假设自来水温度约为20摄氏度，并且有1000立方厘米的水需要升高80度，

cues.en: then it will take 80,000
cues.zh: 那就要花 80,000

cues.en: calories of energy to bring it to a boil.
cues.zh: 卡路里的能量才能把它烧开。

cues.en: Now we can ask a search engine to convert that into a different unit for us. Let's go with joules.
cues.zh: 现在我们可以让搜索引擎把它换算成另一种单位。就用焦耳吧。

cues.en: No I didn't want the kilocalorie.
cues.zh: 不，我不想要千卡。

cues.en: That's what we commonly use for food.
cues.zh: 那是我们通常用来做食物的东西。

cues.en: I just want 80,000
cues.zh: 我只想要 8 万

cues.en: calories, the regular kind.
cues.zh: 卡路里，普通的那种。

cues.en: Fine.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: 80 kilocalories is 334,720
joules.
cues.zh: 焦耳。

cues.en: Why have I chosen joules? Well, here's a fun thing. You know what the watt, the commonly used unit of electrical power, actually is?
cues.zh: 我为什么选择焦耳呢？这里有件有意思的事。你知道瓦特这个常用的电功率单位究竟是什么吗？

cues.en: It's one joule per second.
cues.zh: 这就是每秒一焦耳。

cues.en: And since our electric kettles typically run at 1,500 watts, that means they can put 1,500
cues.zh: 而我们的电水壶通常功率是1500瓦，这意味着它们能输出1500

cues.en: joules of energy into the water every second.
cues.zh: 焦耳的能量每秒注入水中。

cues.en: So if we divide 334,720,
cues.zh: 所以，如果我们用334,720来除，

cues.en: the number of joules we need, by 1,500,
cues.zh: 我们需要的焦耳数，除以 1,500，

cues.en: the number of joules we can add to the water every second, we will find out how much time it should take for an electric kettle in The US to boil a liter of room temperature water in seconds.
cues.zh: 我们每秒钟能给水加多少焦耳，就能算出美国电水壶烧开一升室温水需要多少秒。

cues.en: Bad answer?

cues.en: Two hundred twenty three.
cues.zh: 二百二十三。

cues.en: In the real world, though, it took about twenty two percent longer than that. Our theoretical speed is two hundred twenty three seconds but the observed time was two hundred seventy three seconds.

cues.en: What's the cause of the discrepancy?
cues.zh: 造成这种差异的原因是什么？

cues.en: Well actually there are two causes. First, this thing doesn't actually pull 1,500 watts from the wall.
cues.zh: 实际上有两个原因。首先，这东西从墙上的插座实际消耗的并不是 1500 瓦。

cues.en: It's a resistive electrical load, the heating element is just a giant resistor after all, so the actual power it consumes will depend on the voltage at the receptacle.
cues.zh: 它是一个电阻性负载，加热元件说到底也就是个巨大的电阻，所以它实际消耗的功率取决于插座的电压。

cues.en: In my test it was drawing only fourteen
cues.zh: 在我的测试中，它只消耗了十四

cues.en: thirty watts.
cues.zh: 三十瓦。

cues.en: Knowing that this was the real power output, our theoretical time should be revised to two hundred thirty four seconds.
cues.zh: 知道了这是实际功率输出后，我们的理论时间应该修正为二百三十四秒。

cues.en: Our observed time, though, was still about 16% longer than that. Why?
cues.zh: 不过，我们实际观测到的时间仍然比它长了约 16%。为什么？

cues.en: Well, it's not just the water that we're heating. The body of the kettle itself gets warmed up through the water and that thermal mass slows us down a bit.

cues.en: Plus, of course, some energy escapes into the room before the water boils, both through the sides getting warm and a bit escaping out the top.
cues.zh: 另外，当然了，在水烧开之前，有一部分能量会散失到房间里，既通过壶身变热散失，也有一部分从顶部跑掉了。

cues.en: Still though, only 16% more time compared to literal perfection

cues.en: ain't bad.

cues.en: Let's switch things up a bit. Remember, energy is energy, and we can convert the 80,000 calories it takes to lift a liter of water by 80 degrees
cues.zh: 我们换个角度。记住，能量就是能量，我们可以把将一升水升高 80 度所需的 8 万卡路里

cues.en: into watt hours.
cues.zh: 转化为瓦时。

cues.en: Joules are fun and all, but since we tend to measure power output in watts it's usually easier to conceptualize energy in watt hours.
cues.zh: 焦耳挺好玩，不过既然我们习惯用瓦特衡量功率，通常用瓦时来理解能量会更容易。

cues.en: Plus you get much smaller numbers which is helpful.
cues.zh: 而且数字会小得多，这很有帮助。

cues.en: 80,000 calories is about 93 watt hours according to Google's converti thing.
cues.zh: 根据谷歌那个换算小工具，80,000卡路里大约是93瓦时。

cues.en: How many watt hours did our kettle use?
cues.zh: 我们的电水壶用了多少瓦时？

cues.en: Well, two hundred seventy three seconds divided by the thirty six hundred seconds in an hour and then multiplied by the fourteen
cues.zh: 嗯，273秒除以一小时的3,600秒，再乘以14

cues.en: thirty watts the kettle was actually pulling tells us that we consumed
cues.zh: 30瓦——也就是电水壶实际消耗的功率——告诉我们，我们消耗了

cues.en: watt hours which is,
cues.zh: 瓦时，也就是，

cues.en: what do you know, about 16% more than 93. Ain't this fun?
cues.zh: 真没想到，比93多了大约16%。是不是挺好玩？

cues.en: Let's do a little more math. Through the magic of buying two of them, I have a second slightly fancier kettle, and this one sports rapid heat technology.
cues.zh: 我们再算一点。多亏我买了两个，我还有第二个稍微高级点的电水壶，这个主打快速加热技术。

cues.en: Which is funny because it's only rated 1,100 watts. This one has the embedded heating element design. Rather than a big curly thing getting hot, the bottom surface is what gets hot.
cues.zh: 有意思的是，它标称只有1,100瓦。这个用的是嵌入式加热元件设计。不是一大团卷曲的东西发热，而是底部表面发热。

cues.en: Given what we've learned, we should be able to predict how long this will take to boil a liter of water.
cues.zh: 根据我们刚学到的，应该能预测它烧开一升水要多久。

cues.en: Let's see, 334,720
joules divided by 1,100 watts is three hundred four seconds or just over five minutes.
cues.zh: 焦耳除以1,100瓦是304秒，也就是刚过5分钟。

cues.en: I'll go ahead and presume the same 22 overall discrepancy from the cheap kettle accounting for both a slightly lower than advertised power level and also the energy needed to heat the kettle itself and predict it should take about three hundred seventy one seconds, or six minutes and eleven seconds.
cues.zh: 我就先假设和那个便宜水壶一样，有22%的总体偏差——把实际功率略低于标称、以及加热水壶本身所需的能量都算进去——然后预测它大概需要371秒，也就是6分11秒。

cues.en: Let's see how long does it actually take?
cues.zh: 看看它实际需要多长时间？

cues.en: Oh good, blue LEDs.
cues.zh: 太好了，蓝色LED。

cues.en: My favorite.
cues.zh: 我的最爱。

cues.en: And it actually took six minutes and thirteen seconds, proving once again that energy is energy and water is water.
cues.zh: 结果真花了六分十三秒，再次证明了能量就是能量，水就是水。

cues.en: So now let's take a look at the gas stove and stovetop kettle again.
cues.zh: 那么现在我们再来看看燃气灶和炉台上的水壶。

cues.en: The burner which took seven minutes and forty seconds to bring this to a boil is rated 9,500
cues.zh: 这个炉头烧开这锅水用了7分40秒，额定功率是9500

cues.en: BTUs per hour.
cues.zh: 每小时英热单位。

cues.en: Oh good. Another unit.
cues.zh: 哦，太好了。又一个单元。

cues.en: Now in this context, as is often done with the BTU for whatever reason, the manufacturer is using a unit of energy to convey power which is a bit confusing but it is what it is. I don't have a way to verify its performance unfortunately,
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，就像人们出于某种原因常对 BTU 所做的那样，厂商在用能量单位来表达功率，这有点让人困惑，但事实就是如此。不幸的是，我没办法验证它的性能，

cues.en: but if we assume the burner is performing to spec the 9,500 BTUs per hour can be converted to instantaneous wattage
cues.zh: 但如果假设炉头符合标称性能，每小时 9500 BTU 就可以换算成瞬时功率

cues.en: and thus this burner outputs 2,785
cues.zh: 因此这个 burner 输出 2,785

cues.en: watts at full power.
cues.zh: 满功率时的瓦数。

cues.en: You may already see the absurdity here but let's keep going and work it out. It should take only ninety three watt hours to bring a liter of water to boil.
cues.zh: 你可能已经看出这里的荒谬之处，但我们继续往下推。把一升水烧开应该只需要九十三瓦时。

cues.en: This electric kettle, with a modest loss, took 108.4
cues.zh: 这个电热水壶损耗不大，耗时 108.4

cues.en: watt hours to do it. The second electric kettle with a lower power rating did take longer to do the job but required a nearly identical amount of energy.
cues.zh: 瓦时来完成。第二款额定功率较低的电热水壶确实花了更长时间，但消耗的能量几乎完全相同。

cues.en: This thing sitting over 2,785
cues.zh: 这东西停在 2,785 以上

cues.en: watts of fire manages to take more time to boil than either electric kettle. Seven minutes and forty seconds.
cues.zh: Watts of Fire 烧开水竟然比任何一款电水壶都慢，用了7分40秒。

cues.en: That works out to 356
cues.zh: 算下来是 356

cues.en: watt hours of energy consumed.
cues.zh: 消耗的瓦时能量。

cues.en: That's astoundingly
cues.zh: 这简直是

cues.en: bad, nearly quadruple what's theoretically required and more than triple what the electric kettles need.
cues.zh: 糟透了，几乎是理论所需值的四倍，比电热水壶所需的多出两倍还多。

cues.en: But it's not really surprising, is it? I mean, this is just a cold object over an open flame. Of course the bulk of the energy being released as the fuel combusts
cues.zh: 但这其实并不让人意外，对吧？我的意思是，这只是明火上的一个冰冷物体。燃料燃烧释放的大部分能量

cues.en: is just going around the kettle.
cues.zh: 自然都散失到水壶周围了。

cues.en: If you've ever used a gas stove you've undoubtedly felt how hot the air is above the pot or whatever.
cues.zh: 如果你用过燃气灶，你肯定能感觉到锅具上方空气有多热。

cues.en: That's all the heat from the flame which isn't ending up in what you're trying to heat.
cues.zh: 这都是那些没有被传导到你想要加热的物体上的火焰热量。

cues.en: Sure, some of it's making it in there but in the case of this kettle apparently not even a third.
cues.zh: 当然，有一部分进去了，但对于这个水壶来说，显然连三分之一都不到。

cues.en: This stove also sports a quick boil mega burner which outputs 17,000
cues.zh: 这个炉灶还配备了一个速沸超大火力燃烧器，输出功率达 17,000

cues.en: BTUs per hour, or 4,985
cues.zh: BTU/小时，即 4,985

cues.en: watts.
cues.zh: 瓦。

cues.en: This thing is so powerful flames lick up the sides of the kettle.
cues.zh: 这玩意儿火力太猛了，火焰都舔舐着水壶的侧壁。

cues.en: On this mega burner, the time to boil decreases to four minutes and thirty two seconds,
cues.zh: 在这个超大火力燃烧器上，烧开水的时间缩短到了 4 分 32 秒，

cues.en: which as it happens is exactly one second faster than the time recorded by this electric kettle.
cues.zh: 碰巧的是，这比这个电热水壶记录的时间快了整整一秒。

cues.en: But that time saving comes with even less efficiency,
cues.zh: 但这种时间节省带来的是更低的效率，

cues.en: as the total amount of energy needed to boil a liter of water on this burner climbs slightly from 356
cues.zh: 因为在这个燃烧器上烧开一升水所需的总能量从 356

cues.en: to 376
cues.zh: 微微上升到了 376

cues.en: watt hours.
cues.zh: 瓦时。

cues.en: Oh and by the way, 376
cues.zh: 哦对了，376

cues.en: watt hours isn't just a lot of energy to spend boiling a liter of water, it'll also make your kitchen quite a bit warmer which is great on summer days.
cues.zh: 瓦时不仅是烧开一升水所需的大量能量，还会让你的厨房变得相当暖和，这在夏天真是太棒了。

cues.en: Oh, also the heat from the flames licking up the sides makes the handle too hot to touch with bare hands so that's fun.
cues.zh: 哦，还有，火焰舔舐壶壁产生的热量让把手烫得无法赤手触摸，真是太有趣了。

cues.en: There's been a lot of talk lately about how gas stoves are just,
cues.zh: 最近很多人都在讨论燃气灶到底有多……

cues.en: well, kinda bad for lots of reasons, and I gotta say this is revealing yet another reason.
cues.zh: 呃，出于种种原因确实挺糟糕的，而我得说，这又暴露了另一个缺点。

cues.en: I mean, if it takes more than triple the energy output of a 1,500 watt electric kettle just to match its boiling time,
cues.zh: 我是说，如果它要消耗1500瓦电水壶三倍以上的能量，才能达到相同的烧水速度，

cues.en: all I can say is yikes.
cues.zh: 那我只能说，这也太离谱了。

cues.en: Let's go back to the electric stove and see how well it did from an efficiency standpoint.
cues.zh: 我们再回过头来看看电炉，从能效的角度看它表现如何。

cues.en: If we assume that this burner was outputting 2,000 watts, then the required time of exactly six minutes, which is exactly one tenth of an hour, meant 200 watt hours were spent boiling the liter of water.
cues.zh: 假设这个炉头的输出功率是2000瓦，用时刚好六分钟，也就是十分之一小时，意味着烧开这一升水消耗了200瓦时。

cues.en: That's still much more than the electric kettle's 108,
cues.zh: 虽然这还是远高于电水壶的108瓦时，

cues.en: but nowhere near as bad as the 356
cues.zh: 但远没有慢速燃气灶

cues.en: required by the slower gas burner.
cues.zh: 所需的356瓦时那么夸张。

cues.en: Putting the kettle in physical contact with the thing that gets hot seems to transfer heat energy much more effectively.
cues.zh: 让水壶直接接触发热体，热量传递显然要高效得多。

cues.en: For grins and giggles, I timed this little hot plate.
cues.zh: 为了好玩，我还测了这个小电热板。

cues.en: It only outputs 900 watts so it took
cues.zh: 它的功率只有900瓦，所以花了

cues.en: a while. Thirteen minutes and eight seconds, in fact.
cues.zh: 挺长时间。实际上用了13分8秒。

cues.en: Let's do the math, though. This thing really only outputs about 870
cues.zh: 不过我们来算一下。根据功率计测得，这东西实际输出其实只有大约870

cues.en: watts according to the kilowatt.
cues.zh: 瓦。

cues.en: Thirteen minutes and eight seconds at that power level works out to 190
cues.zh: 在这个功率下运行13分8秒，算下来是190

cues.en: watt hours.
cues.zh: 瓦时。

cues.en: This was definitely
cues.zh: 速度上确实

cues.en: slower than the two kilowatt burner but it was a tad more efficient. At least, I assume so. Probably because the glass ceramic cooktop works almost like a heat lamp pointing up at the kettle.
cues.zh: 比2000瓦的炉头慢，但能效稍微高了一点。至少我是这么认为的。可能是因为微晶玻璃面板就像一盏向上对着水壶照射的加热灯。

cues.en: It's blasting infrared light at it, and since the kettle is just a little bit smaller than the total area, some energy is making its way around the kettle's sides.
cues.zh: 它向水壶发射红外光，由于水壶比总面积稍微小一点，一部分能量会绕到水壶的侧面。

cues.en: This burner, though, is simply getting real hot thanks to a heating element inside of it, and with the kettle in physical contact a slight majority of that energy ends up getting absorbed by the kettle and into the water.
cues.zh: 不过，这个炉头内部有加热元件，加热后会变得非常烫，水壶与其直接接触，其中绝大部分能量最终被水壶吸收并传递给水。

cues.en: Not bad.
cues.zh: 还不错。

cues.en: This probably means that the old fashioned curly q burners might actually be the best conventional electric burner design,
cues.zh: 这可能意味着，老式的螺旋形电热盘实际上可能是传统电炉的最佳设计，

cues.en: at least when it comes to speed since they have relatively little thermal mass and the element itself stays in contact with the cookware.
cues.zh: 至少在速度方面是这样，因为它们的蓄热量相对较小，且加热元件本身一直与厨具保持接触。

cues.en: With everything we've seen, I think it's clear that if you want to boil water conveniently and quickly,
cues.zh: 结合我们看到的一切，我认为很明显，如果你想方便快捷地烧水，

cues.en: the electric kettle remains your best option despite our weedy little plugs.
cues.zh: 尽管我们的插头功率不大，但电热水壶依然是你的最佳选择。

cues.en: But this may be about to change.
cues.zh: 不过这种情况可能快要改变了。

cues.en: Thanks to induction technology,
cues.zh: 多亏了电磁感应技术，

cues.en: the stovetop kettle can be even faster than an electric kettle, in fact potentially faster than a European one.
cues.zh: 炉灶水壶甚至可以比电热水壶更快，实际上可能比欧洲的电热水壶还要快。

cues.en: Induction stoves are the new hotness,
cues.zh: 电磁炉是新近的热门技术，

cues.en: and they work by sending high frequency alternating current through a coil of wire beneath the cooking surface.
cues.zh: 它们的工作原理是通过烹饪表面下方的线圈发送高频交流电。

cues.en: When a suitable cooking vessel is placed above it, electric currents are induced within the vessel's metal base.
cues.zh: 当把合适的炊具放在上方时，会在炊具的金属底部感应出电流。

cues.en: Those currents will actually heat the bottom of the pot or what have you just like the current flowing through a heating element.
cues.zh: 这些电流实际上会加热锅底或类似的东西，就像电流流过加热元件一样。

cues.en: In effect,
cues.zh: 实际上，

cues.en: it turns the pot itself
cues.zh: 它会把锅本身

cues.en: into the heating element.
cues.zh: 变成加热元件。

cues.en: Now, I don't have an induction stove,
cues.zh: 我没有电磁炉，

cues.en: but I do have this plug in induction cooktop.
cues.zh: 但我有这台插电式电磁炉。

cues.en: This thing is not shy of pulling the full 15 amps from an electrical circuit, and on full power it consumes just about the 1,800 watts that it claims to.
cues.zh: 这东西会毫不客气地从电路中拉取满载15安培的电流，开到最大功率时，耗电量确实约为它标称的1800瓦。

cues.en: Now, there's some waste in this process, that's why this thing has a cooling fan in it, so I don't know exactly how much is actually getting transmitted into the kettle.
cues.zh: 这个过程会有一些能量损耗，所以它里面装了一个散热风扇。因此我不确定究竟有多少能量真正传递到了水壶里。

cues.en: But at full power this brought a liter of water to boil in four minutes and twenty nine seconds.
cues.zh: 但在最大功率下，它用了4分29秒把一升水烧开。

cues.en: That's the fastest result we've seen suggesting at least 1,500 watts is making it into the water.
cues.zh: 这是我们测到的最快结果，这至少说明有1500瓦的功率传进了水里。

cues.en: And keep in mind this is limited to what comes from an ordinary electrical outlet.
cues.zh: 还要注意，这受限于普通电源插座能提供的功率。

cues.en: The hardwired induction cooktops you'll find either on their own or attached to an oven often feature a burner or I guess a better word is
cues.zh: 你在独立安装或和烤箱连在一起的嵌入式电磁炉上，通常会看到一个炉区，或者更准确地说，

cues.en: emitter, that can pump out close to four kilowatts,
cues.zh: 一个能输出接近4千瓦的发射器，

cues.en: sometimes more.
cues.zh: 有时甚至更高。

cues.en: With one of those you could boil a liter of water in ninety seconds flat.
cues.zh: 用这种设备，你可以在整整90秒内烧开一升水。

cues.en: Still, speed isn't everything.
cues.zh: 不过，速度并不是一切。

cues.en: One very handy feature of nearly all electric kettles is that automatic shut off. That does give them an element of safety which is missing from a stovetop kettle.
cues.zh: 几乎所有电热水壶都有一个非常实用的功能，那就是自动断电。这确实让它们具备了炉灶水壶所没有的一层安全保障。

cues.en: I think there's a certain charm in household objects that scream at you when they're ready,
cues.zh: 我觉得，家居用品烧开后用声音提醒你，还是挺有魅力的，

cues.en: but I'll admit a more silent option is
cues.zh: 但我得承认，更安静的选择

cues.en: nice.
cues.zh: 确实不错。

cues.en: Plus, unless and until I get a proper induction stove,
cues.zh: 另外，除非我换上一台像样的电磁炉，

cues.en: this remains the fastest...
cues.zh: 否则它依然是最快的……

cues.en: Okay. This was a little bit faster but the most convenient and efficient option for boiling water.
cues.zh: 行吧。这个稍微快了一点，但依然是烧水最方便、最高效的选择。

cues.en: Though I don't often drink tea, I've kept a kettle around because it's just too handy. Even if I'm making pasta,
cues.zh: 虽然我不常喝茶，但我一直留着个水壶，因为它实在太顺手了。哪怕我要煮意面，

cues.en: it's faster to fill this up, bring it to a boil, and then pour the water from it into a pot on the stove than it is to use the stove to boil the water.
cues.zh: 也是先把水灌满烧开，再把水倒进炉子上的锅里，比直接用炉子烧水还要快。

cues.en: Which is nuts but it's the truth.
cues.zh: 这虽然挺离谱，但确实是事实。

cues.en: Plus the kitchen doesn't get nearly as hot when you do that and I don't have to run the stove as long which is great for indoor air quality.
cues.zh: 而且这样做厨房没那么热，我也不用开那么久炉灶，这对室内空气质量太棒了。

cues.en: I should make a video about that too. It's astounding how bad these are. It's almost like combusting fossil fuels inside of a living space is a bad idea.
cues.zh: 我也该拍个关于这个的视频。这东西有多糟糕简直惊人。在起居空间里燃烧化石燃料，听上去就像是个馊主意。

cues.en: Aside from that great benefit, there are also fancier kettles available which let you set them to a specific temperature.
cues.zh: 除了这个大好处之外，市面上还有更高级的水壶，可以让你设定特定的温度。

cues.en: Great for certain types of tea or really pedantic coffee snop I mean enthusiasts.
cues.zh: 这非常适合某些种类的茶，或是非常严谨的咖啡发烧友——我是说爱好者。

cues.en: And if you're really bothered by waiting four minutes for boiled water, there are a few solutions that are much less involved than rewiring your kitchen.
cues.zh: 如果你真的嫌等四分钟水开太煎熬，还有一些比重新走厨房电路简单得多的方案。

cues.en: First, and here's a wild idea,
cues.zh: 首先，有个挺疯狂的想法，

cues.en: just don't fill the kettle up all the way. It takes more time to boil more water,
cues.zh: 就是别把水壶加太满。水越多烧的时间越长，

cues.en: and if you're just making a cup for yourself,
cues.zh: 如果你只是给自己泡一杯，

cues.en: only fill the kettle to the minimum mark. On many kettles that can be as little as half a liter which only takes a hair over two minutes to boil even with our pathetic little plugs.
cues.zh: 水壶加到最低水位线就行。很多水壶最低只需半升水，哪怕用我们那可怜的小插座，也只要稍微多过两分钟就能烧开。

cues.en: But watch out as there are kettles out there which don't operate at 1,500 watts.
cues.zh: 但要注意，市面上有些电热水壶并不是1500瓦的。

cues.en: Like this one.
cues.zh: 比如这个。

cues.en: It may look nicer than the cheap Walmart kettle,
cues.zh: 它可能比沃尔玛那个便宜的壶好看，

cues.en: but it's definitely worse at being a kettle.
cues.zh: 但作为电热水壶，它绝对更差劲。

cues.en: Oh but it did come with this free loose leaf tea infuser so that's nice.
cues.zh: 哦，不过它附带了这个免费的散叶茶滤网，这点还不错。

cues.en: Another option you might want to look into if you're particularly impatient is something like this.
cues.zh: 如果你特别没耐心，另一个值得考虑的选择是这样的东西。

cues.en: You're right, this isn't a kettle but you could call it better than a kettle.
cues.zh: 你说得对，这不算电热水壶，但你可以说它比电热水壶更好。

cues.en: These...
cues.zh: 这些……

cues.en: Well I don't know what the proper name is but boiler, warmer, and dispenser all seem like common words so let's go with hot water dispenser.
cues.zh: 我不知道它准确的名称，但boiler、warmer和dispenser似乎都是常见叫法，那就叫它热水机吧。

cues.en: These hot water dispensers feature an insulated tank which they will diligently keep at your desired temperature.
cues.zh: 这些热水机有一个保温水箱，会持续把水保持在你的目标温度。

cues.en: Many also feature timer functions to allow you to set when you want them ready so they don't waste much energy when you don't need them.
cues.zh: 很多还有定时功能，让你设定何时准备好，这样不需要时就不会浪费太多电。

cues.en: Use one of these and you don't ever have to wait for a kettle, and they actually only need 700 watts.
